WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: likely a worn fill‑valve seal causing the underfill alarm (most common cause per SOP, work instruction, NCR, and knowledge graph)  
- What is different: this is the first underfill alarm on 29 Oct 2026 and is not linked to the specific valves (9, 15, 3) that leaked on 10 Sep 2026; therefore a new occurrence of the same fault type.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: line stopped for inspection/repair; estimated downtime ≈ 1 hour (including sanitation rinse and first‑bottle check)

- Financial impact: downtime cost proportional to 1 hour of line loss; exact dollar amount not provided in sources

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH – fault requires LOTO before any inspection or repair and may lead to a production stop; this meets the “any fault requiring LOTO” HIGH minimum rule.  
- Justification: SOP mandates LOTO for inspection/cleaning; the alarm is the most common fault on FL‑101 and can trigger a systemic stop if recurring.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
Immediate action (numbered steps – safety first, then fix, then verify):
Step 1: Safety — Press the normal STOP button (do NOT use emergency stop unless danger present).  
Step 2: Safety — Apply LOTO per SAF‑003 before any physical inspection or cleaning.  
Step 3: Diagnosis — Read the checkweigher report to identify the under‑filling valve number(s).  
Step 4: Diagnosis — Inspect the identified valve(s):
   - If the valve is dripping, this indicates a worn seal; call maintenance to replace the seal kit (WI‑FL101‑001).  
   - If no dripping, lock out the machine (already LOTO) and clean the nozzle of that valve.  
Step 5: Diagnosis — Verify product supply pressure (Section 12.4 of SOP).  
Step 6: Do NOT increase the fill‑time setting (factory set 3.2 s) – prohibited by SOP and NCR.  
Step 7: If three or more underfill alarms occur in the same shift, raise a maintenance work order and notify the maintenance supervisor (per SOP systemic rule).  
Step 8: Fix — After seal replacement or nozzle cleaning, perform the mandatory sanitation rinse (10 min water rinse).  
Step 9: Verify — Conduct the mandatory first‑bottle check: run 20 bottles, all must weigh 495‑505 ml; stop and re‑inspect if any out of range.  
Step 10: Quality — Shift supervisor signs off the first‑bottle check; record seal kit part number (SEAL‑FV‑24), valve number, and date in the maintenance log.

Root cause fix (permanent solution):
- Replace any worn fill‑valve seals with SEAL‑FV‑24 kits according to WI‑FL101‑001; enforce the 3‑month / 1,500‑hour replacement interval.

Preventive action (stops recurrence):
- Monitor checkweigher early‑warning (>1 reject/100 bottles per hour) and alert shift lead.  
- Enforce “no operator fill‑time changes” rule; any change requires engineering approval.  
- Maintain a minimum stock of 10 seal kits in the spares cabinet.  
- Schedule proactive seal inspections at the defined interval.  
- Provide refresher training on SOP steps and LOTO requirements.

Who to notify:
- Maintenance Supervisor (for seal replacement or nozzle cleaning)  
- Shift Lead (to log the alarm and coordinate stop)  
- Quality Lead (to record the incident and verify first‑bottle results)

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

10. TROUBLESHOOTING AFTER THE JOB

  What you see                        Check                     Action
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Valve still drips                   Seal seated correctly?    Refit the seal
  Valve still underfills, no drip     Nozzle blocked?           Clean the nozzle
  All valves underfill                Supply pressure?          SOP Section 12.4
  Overfill for 2 to 3 minutes only    Normal settling           No action
  Overfill after 5 minutes            Valve fully clicked in?   Refit the valve
  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

11. SIGN-OFF

12.1 Underfill
Alarm message: "Fill level low — bottles under target volume"
The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

This is the most common alarm on FL-101. Causes, most common first:
  1. Worn fill valve seal — the valve drips between fills
  2. Blocked fill nozzle — debris in the nozzle, no dripping
  3. Low product supply pressure — see Section 12.4

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Following this SOP keeps people safe, keeps every bottle within the
declared fill amount, and keeps glass and other foreign objects out of the
product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Causes, most common first:
  1. Guide rails not reset after a bottle size changeover — check the

running. Stop the machine and lock it out (Section 6.2) before clearing
any jam.

  Step 5 — Remove any chipped or damaged bottles from the infeed.
  Step 6 — Remove the lock, restart at 60 bottles per minute for 2 minutes,

This SOP explains how to run the FL-101 Bottle Filler safely and correctly.
It covers the checks before starting, the start-up sequence, the normal
settings, the checks during the shift, what to do for each alarm, bottle
size changeovers, cleaning, records and shutdown.

6.1 PPE required on Filling Line 1
  - Safety glasses at all times
  - Cut-resistant gloves when handling glass or change parts
  - Hearing protection
  - Safety shoes

6.2 Lockout / tagout (LOTO)
LOTO is required before any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or
reaching into the machine. Follow SAF-003:
  1. Switch off power at the main isolator.
  2. Lock the isolator with your personal padlock.
  3. Tag it with your name and the date.
  4. Try to start the machine to prove it cannot run.
Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it.

6.3 Guards
All guard doors have safety switches. The machine stops if a guard door is
opened. Never bypass or tape over a guard switch.

6.4 Main safety rules
  - Never clear a jam while the machine is running.
  - Never reach past a guard.
  - Never use compressed air near open bottles or broken glass.
  - Keep the floor dry. Report leaks and spills straight away.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

This SOP explains how to run the FL-101 Bottle Filler safely and correctly.
It covers the checks before starting, the start-up sequence, the normal
settings, the checks during the shift, what to do for each alarm, bottle
size changeovers, cleaning, records and shutdown.

12. ALARM RESPONSE PROCEDURES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

12.1 Underfill
Alarm message: "Fill level low — bottles under target volume"
The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

This is the most common alarm on FL-101. Causes, most common first:
  1. Worn fill valve seal — the valve drips between fills
  2. Blocked fill nozzle — debris in the nozzle, no dripping
  3. Low product supply pressure — see Section 12.4

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

12.4 Product Supply Pressure Low
Alarm message: "Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar"

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP.
  Step 2 — Clean the supply filter.
  Step 3 — Bleed air from the supply line.
  Step 4 — Confirm the pressure is back to 1.5 to 2.0 bar.
  Step 5 — Restart, then weigh the first 20 bottles. All must be 495 to 505 ml.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

If a bottle breaks during a jam, stop and follow Section 12.3.

12.3 Glass Breakage
Alarm message: "Glass breakage detected in filler"

CRITICAL — broken glass can end up inside filled bottles. This is a
product safety event. Follow GBP-001.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Stop the line at once with the emergency stop.
  Step 2 — Do not open any guard until the machine has stopped and is
           locked out (Section 6.2).
  Step 3 — Put every bottle filled in the last 30 minutes on hold. Label
           them QA HOLD. Throw away any open bottles within 2 metres of
           the break.
  Step 4 — Clean up with the red glass kit only. Use a vacuum, never
           compressed air (air spreads glass).
  Step 5 — Rinse the filler (sanitation rinse, 10 minutes).
  Step 6 — The quality lead must sign off before the line restarts.
  Step 7 — Record the event in the glass breakage log.

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

Step 9 — SANITATION RINSE — MANDATORY
           Run the sanitation rinse for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant
           and any particles from the new seals. Never skip this step: the
           first bottles would carry lubricant into the product.

  Step 10 — FIRST-BOTTLE CHECK — MANDATORY
           Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles.
           All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml.
           If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.

IMPORTANT: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be
slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is
EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings. The
checkweigher rejects these bottles automatically.

9. INSPECTING THE OLD SEALS

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

10. TROUBLESHOOTING AFTER THE JOB

  What you see                        Check                     Action
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Valve still drips                   Seal seated correctly?    Refit the seal
  Valve still underfills, no drip     Nozzle blocked?           Clean the nozzle
  All valves underfill                Supply pressure?          SOP Section 12.4
  Overfill for 2 to 3 minutes only    Normal settling           No action
  Overfill after 5 minutes            Valve fully clicked in?   Refit the valve
  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: underfill alarm triggered by one or more fill valves delivering less than 495 ml, most commonly due to a worn fill‑valve seal (Knowledge Graph, SOP, NCR) or a blocked nozzle if no drip is observed.
- Difference from history: this is the first underfill alarm on FL‑101 since the three‑alarm event on 10 Sep 2026; no escalation to maintenance has yet occurred and no recent seal‑kit replacement is recorded.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: line stopped for diagnosis; estimated downtime ≈ 1 hour including LOTO, inspection, and first‑bottle check (Knowledge Graph estimate).
- Safety risk: LOW (no hazardous energy or injury reported; standard LOTO and PPE required).
- Financial impact: downtime cost approximated by one hour of lost production plus labor for inspection and possible seal replacement.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH
- Justification: fault requires LOTO before any inspection or cleaning and may lead to a production stop; three‑alarm threshold in a shift would trigger a systemic fault, so the minimum rating is HIGH.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — Press the normal STOP button (do NOT use emergency stop unless danger present). Put on required PPE (safety shoes, cut‑resistant gloves, safety glasses, hearing protection).  
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Open the checkweigher report to identify the under‑filling valve numbers.  
  Step 3: Inspect the identified valve(s):
    • If the valve is dripping between fills → worn seal suspected. Call maintenance to replace the seal kit (WI‑FL101‑001).  
    • If no dripping → lock out the machine (SAF‑003 LOTO), then clean the nozzle of the identified valve.  
  Step 4: Check product‑supply pressure as per SOP Section 12.4.  
  Step 5: Do NOT increase the fill time (explicit prohibition in SOP and NCR).  
  Step 6: After any seal replacement or nozzle cleaning, perform the mandatory sanitation rinse (10 min water) and then the first‑bottle check (first 20 bottles must be 495‑505 ml).  
  Step 7: Once the first‑bottle check passes, remove LOTO, restart the line, and record the activity in the maintenance log.

- Root cause fix (permanent solution):
  • Replace worn fill‑valve seal kit (SEAL‑FV‑24) on any valve that drips, following WI‑FL101‑001 steps 1‑10.  
  • Reset fill time to the factory setting of 3.2 s; do not adjust without engineering approval.

- Preventive action:
  • Enforce the 1 500‑hour / 3‑month seal‑replacement interval and verify compliance in the maintenance schedule.  
  • Maintain a minimum stock of 10 SEAL‑FV‑24 kits in the spares cabinet.  
  • Continue to prohibit operators from changing fill time; reinforce this rule in shift briefings.  
  • Monitor underfill alarm frequency; if three or more occur in a shift, stop production, raise a maintenance work order, and notify the maintenance supervisor (SOP systemic fault rule).

- Who to notify:
  • Maintenance Supervisor (for seal replacement or nozzle cleaning).  
  • Shift Lead (to record stop time and alarm details).

This SOP explains how to run the FL-101 Bottle Filler safely and correctly.
It covers the checks before starting, the start-up sequence, the normal
settings, the checks during the shift, what to do for each alarm, bottle
size changeovers, cleaning, records and shutdown.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. ALARM RESPONSE PROCEDURES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

12.1 Underfill
Alarm message: "Fill level low — bottles under target volume"
The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

This is the most common alarm on FL-101. Causes, most common first:
  1. Worn fill valve seal — the valve drips between fills
  2. Blocked fill nozzle — debris in the nozzle, no dripping
  3. Low product supply pressure — see Section 12.4

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Following this SOP keeps people safe, keeps every bottle within the
declared fill amount, and keeps glass and other foreign objects out of the
product.

This SOP applies to:
  - The FL-101 Bottle Filler on Filling Line 1
  - 500 ml and 330 ml glass bottles
  - Still water only

This SOP does not cover the capper (CP-102) or the labeller (LB-103). They

12.2 Infeed Jam

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

If a bottle breaks during a jam, stop and follow Section 12.3.

12.3 Glass Breakage
Alarm message: "Glass breakage detected in filler"

CRITICAL — broken glass can end up inside filled bottles. This is a
product safety event. Follow GBP-001.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Stop the line at once with the emergency stop.
  Step 2 — Do not open any guard until the machine has stopped and is
           locked out (Section 6.2).
  Step 3 — Put every bottle filled in the last 30 minutes on hold. Label
           them QA HOLD. Throw away any open bottles within 2 metres of
           the break.
  Step 4 — Clean up with the red glass kit only. Use a vacuum, never
           compressed air (air spreads glass).
  Step 5 — Rinse the filler (sanitation rinse, 10 minutes).
  Step 6 — The quality lead must sign off before the line restarts.
  Step 7 — Record the event in the glass breakage log.

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

Step 9 — SANITATION RINSE — MANDATORY
           Run the sanitation rinse for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant
           and any particles from the new seals. Never skip this step: the
           first bottles would carry lubricant into the product.

  Step 10 — FIRST-BOTTLE CHECK — MANDATORY
           Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles.
           All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml.
           If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.

IMPORTANT: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be
slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is
EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings. The
checkweigher rejects these bottles automatically.

9. INSPECTING THE OLD SEALS

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

10. TROUBLESHOOTING AFTER THE JOB

  What you see                        Check                     Action
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Valve still drips                   Seal seated correctly?    Refit the seal
  Valve still underfills, no drip     Nozzle blocked?           Clean the nozzle
  All valves underfill                Supply pressure?          SOP Section 12.4
  Overfill for 2 to 3 minutes only    Normal settling           No action
  Overfill after 5 minutes            Valve fully clicked in?   Refit the valve
  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

11. SIGN-OFF

12.1 Underfill
Alarm message: "Fill level low — bottles under target volume"
The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

This is the most common alarm on FL-101. Causes, most common first:
  1. Worn fill valve seal — the valve drips between fills
  2. Blocked fill nozzle — debris in the nozzle, no dripping
  3. Low product supply pressure — see Section 12.4

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Following this SOP keeps people safe, keeps every bottle within the
declared fill amount, and keeps glass and other foreign objects out of the
product.

- Difference vs historical pattern: Prior jam occurred after a 330 ml bottle changeover and a chipped bottle was identified; the current incident reports no recent changeover and no chipped bottle noted, suggesting the jam may be due solely to an unexpected bottle obstruction rather than a changeover error.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line stopped (FL‑101 infeed jam alarm) – line down until jam cleared.
- Safety risk: HIGH (requires LOTO, reaching into machine, potential for broken glass).
- Financial impact: Not quantified in source data; line downtime implies loss of production capacity.

- HIGH
- Justification: Jam requires LOTO and production stop; safety rules mandate lockout before any jam clearing; recurring jam type (infeed jam) has occurred previously, meeting HIGH minimum.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — Press STOP, then perform LOTO per SAF‑003 (switch off power at main isolator, apply personal lock, tag with name/date, verify machine cannot start).
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Wear cut‑resistant gloves; open guard doors; inspect the star wheel and infeed for jammed bottles and any chipped or damaged bottles.
  Step 3: Fix — Remove jammed bottles manually; if any bottles are chipped or broken, discard them; check guide‑rail position against the bottle size (refer to Changeover sheet CS‑FL101) and lock rails in correct position; ensure the matching star wheel is fitted.
  Step 4: Verify — Remove LOTO, restart machine at 60 bottles per minute for 2 minutes, observe feed for any further blockage, then return to normal speed (120 bpm). Confirm no further alarms.
  Step 5: Quality — Quarantine any bottles removed that show damage; inspect first 20 bottles after restart for fill quality.
- Root cause fix (permanent solution): After any bottle‑size changeover, always verify guide‑rail position and lock; implement a pre‑start visual inspection of the infeed for foreign objects; adjust feed conveyor speed if jams recur.
- Preventive action: Add a checklist item to the shift start‑up sheet to confirm guide‑rail lock and clear infeed; train operators to report any chipped bottles immediately; schedule periodic cleaning of the star wheel area.

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

call the maintenance supervisor.

Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

  Step 1 — Press STOP.
  Step 2 — Clean the supply filter.
  Step 3 — Bleed air from the supply line.
  Step 4 — Confirm the pressure is back to 1.5 to 2.0 bar.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

6. SAFETY

  - Lock out the machine before starting (LOTO, SOP Section 6.2).
  - Wear safety glasses and gloves.
  - Only use food-grade lubricant. Any other lubricant contaminates the
    product.
  - Keep removed parts and tools on the tray. Nothing may be left inside
    the machine.

7. BEFORE YOU START

  - Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling.
  - Mark those valves with a green tag so the right valves are changed.
  - Tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped.

8. PROCEDURE

If a bottle breaks during a jam, stop and follow Section 12.3.

12.3 Glass Breakage
Alarm message: "Glass breakage detected in filler"

CRITICAL — broken glass can end up inside filled bottles. This is a
product safety event. Follow GBP-001.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Stop the line at once with the emergency stop.
  Step 2 — Do not open any guard until the machine has stopped and is
           locked out (Section 6.2).
  Step 3 — Put every bottle filled in the last 30 minutes on hold. Label
           them QA HOLD. Throw away any open bottles within 2 metres of
           the break.
  Step 4 — Clean up with the red glass kit only. Use a vacuum, never
           compressed air (air spreads glass).
  Step 5 — Rinse the filler (sanitation rinse, 10 minutes).
  Step 6 — The quality lead must sign off before the line restarts.
  Step 7 — Record the event in the glass breakage log.

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

FILL VALVE SEAL REPLACEMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

Step 9 — SANITATION RINSE — MANDATORY
           Run the sanitation rinse for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant
           and any particles from the new seals. Never skip this step: the
           first bottles would carry lubricant into the product.

  Step 10 — FIRST-BOTTLE CHECK — MANDATORY
           Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles.
           All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml.
           If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.

IMPORTANT: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be
slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is
EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings. The
checkweigher rejects these bottles automatically.

9. INSPECTING THE OLD SEALS

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

10. TROUBLESHOOTING AFTER THE JOB

  What you see                        Check                     Action
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Valve still drips                   Seal seated correctly?    Refit the seal
  Valve still underfills, no drip     Nozzle blocked?           Clean the nozzle
  All valves underfill                Supply pressure?          SOP Section 12.4
  Overfill for 2 to 3 minutes only    Normal settling           No action
  Overfill after 5 minutes            Valve fully clicked in?   Refit the valve
  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

11. SIGN-OFF

This SOP explains how to run the FL-101 Bottle Filler safely and correctly.
It covers the checks before starting, the start-up sequence, the normal
settings, the checks during the shift, what to do for each alarm, bottle
size changeovers, cleaning, records and shutdown.

Record every check on the pre-start checklist. The shift lead signs it.

8.1 Fill valves and seals
  - Look at each of the 24 fill valves for cracks or dripping.
  - A valve that drips between fills has a worn seal. Report it before
    starting.
  - Seal kits (part SEAL-FV-24) are replaced every 3 months or every
    1,500 running hours, whichever comes first.
  - Spare seal kits are kept in the Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2.
    The minimum stock is 10 kits.

8.2 Infeed and guide rails
  - Check the guide rails are set for the bottle size being run:
      500 ml bottles: rail position A
      330 ml bottles: rail position B
  - Check the rails are locked and the matching star wheel is fitted.

8.3 Product supply
  - Check the bowl level indicator shows NORMAL.
  - Check the product supply pressure is 1.5 to 2.0 bar.
  - The supply filter (part FLT-PS-10) is cleaned once a week. Check the
    date on the filter tag.

Following this SOP keeps people safe, keeps every bottle within the
declared fill amount, and keeps glass and other foreign objects out of the
product.

  - The FL-101 Bottle Filler on Filling Line 1
  - 500 ml and 330 ml glass bottles
  - Still water only

This SOP does not cover the capper (CP-102) or the labeller (LB-103). They

3. RESPONSIBILITIES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  - Completes the pre-start checks and the checks during the shift
  - Responds to alarms and records them in the shift log
  - Stops the machine if anything looks unsafe

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the

  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
